3G-RNC|RNC_101c.Formula Note: The counter values are given in standardised RSSI values (0-621). This means that the values must be converted to dBm values (-112.1 - -50.0) before the KPI can be calculated. It is possible that the counter in the formula is not updated during the measurement period, meaning that the denominator counter is not updated. These samples should be filtered out. When using the formula, linear scale has to be used with calculations. This means that the dBm values in the counters must be converted to Watts and, after the calculation is done, the result must be converted back to dBms.

3G-RNC|RNC_177c.Description in release WCDMA 21: Average PrxNoise [dBm] of a cell over the reporting period.
3G-RNC|RNC_177c.Formula Note:
Note 1: When using the formula, linear scale has to be used with calculations. This means that the dBm values in the counters must be converted to Watts and after the calculation is done, the result must be converted back to dBms. It is possible that the counter in the formula is not updated during the measurement period, that is, the denominator counter is not updated. These samples should be filtered out. The calculation must also include a division by - 100 in order to take out the raw counter unit value multiplication by -100. 
Note 2: Pre-calculated values The counter M1000C10 already shows the average dBm level. Therefore, the denom counter M1000C11 is not used in the formula.

3G-RNC|RNC_605b.Description:
The accessibility of all started resource allocations for HS-DSCH for NRT Traffic. 
The number of times when HS-DSCH channel has been established divided by the number of times when HS-DSCH channel has been selected by cell specific PS.

3G-RNC|RNC_605b.Description in release WCDMA 21:
The accessibility of all started resource allocations for HS-DSCH for NRT Traffic. 
The number of times when HS-DSCH channel has been established divided by the number of times when HS-DSCH channel has been selected by cell specific PS.
3G-RNC|RNC_605b.Note:
Note1: The times that the DCH is selected due to high R99 power is not included in the formula.
Note2: In case HSPA queueing and resource rotation are in use (RAN3110), there might be both failed and successful counter updates for a single request. This is because the feature makes it possible during the reservation process to find a resource for an already rejected resource request. As the KPI counts both requests, a lower success rate than the actual is reflected.

3G-RNC|RNC_722d.Description:
The average active HS-DSCH MAC-d cell throughput from network perspective calculated as the HSDPA MAC-d throughput at BTS divided by the active HS-DSCH time from the network perspective. 
The active time refers to the scheduled TTIs, i.e. when sending data. 
The throughput is looked at from MAC-d layer, i.e. how much MAC-d level
data the HS-DSCH is able to successfully transfer to UEs using the scheduled
TTIs, so this considers also the MAC-hs efficiency.
When aggregated per BTS and higher this KPIs is still showing average Cell
throughput for all Cells.

3G-RNC|RNC_732b.Description:
This KPI shows the outgoing ATM layer traffic load for single ATM VC connection. 
The load is measured in RNC egress direction. 
It depends on the selected configuration, which traffic type utilises one VCC. 
The ATM VCC traffic throughput is compared to the VCC PCR (in the case of CBR connection) or MDCR (in the case of UBR+ connection) to calculate the load [%]. 
If there is dedicated VC connection used for HSDPA, this KPI can be used to follow the HSDPA load over Iub and the same applies to other traffic types as well.

3G-RNC|RNC_913b.Description in release WCDMA 21:
The accessibility of all started resource allocations for E-DCH for NRT Traffic. 
The number of times when E-DCH channel has been established divided by the number of times when HS-DSCH channel has been selected by cell specific PS.
3G-RNC|RNC_913b.Note:
1. This KPI includes all reservations, also all SHO branches included in HSUPA AS.
2. The corresponding IHSPA KPI is IHSPA5005a
3. In case HSPA queueing and resource rotation are in use (RAN3110), there might be both failed and successful counter updates for a single request. This is because the feature makes it possible during the reservation process to find a resource for an already rejected resource request. As the KPI counts both requests, a lower success rate than the actual is reflected.

3G-RNC|RNC_1879e.Description:
The average active HS-DSCH MAC-d throughput from end user perspective, calculated
as the HSDPA MAC-d throughput at BTS, divided by the active HS-DSCH time
multiplied by the active users.  

The active time refers to the scheduled TTIs, i.e. when sending data. 
The active users refers to the number of users with data in the allocated buffer. 
Allocated buffer means that the users are scheduled or waiting to be scheduled in a TTI.

The throughput is looked at from MAC-d layer, i.e. how much MAC-d level
data the HS-DSCH is able to successfully transfer to UEs using the scheduled
TTIs, so this considers also the MAC-hs efficiency.

3G-RNC|RNC_5204a.Formula Note:
IuB PS Throughput = ((T_PS*1.11- T_HSDPA)*(1+SHO_OH) + T_HSDPA), where 1.11 is FP overhead. 

T_PS - Iu-PS average throughput in downlink direction. This KPI results from the combination of GTP-U throughput and Iu-PS throughput counted at NP8S1 or NP2GE interfaces unit, providing the whole figure for combined Iu-PS throughput.

T-HSPA - HSDPA throughput on frame protocol level.

SHO_OH - Soft Handover Overhead in SRNC

CS_Erl - CS Voice, Erlangs.

3G-RNC|RNC_5221a.Description:
The used AAL2 connectivity in RNC196 is the sum of AAL2 path configured cell rates on Iub, Iur and Iu.
M550C0 (AAL2_PATH_GUAR_CELL_RATE) is the configured cell rate for the ATM VCC. For CBR type VC connections this is the AAL2 VCC Peak Cell rate (PCR). For UBR+ VCC in a bundle, this is the PCR of the bundle. For UBR+ VCC not in a bundle, this is the Minimum Desired Cell Rate (MDCR) of the VCC.

3G-RNC|RNC_5234a.Description in release WCDMA 21: RNC Control Plane load factor, as a sum of relevant control plane events for RAN services: SRB service setup, Single or Multi RAB service setup, transport channel setup and maintenance (including channel type switches, HSPA serving cell changes).
3G-RNC|RNC_5234a.Note:
The KPI counts also some RAN Service related events that doesn't require NBAP signaling:
-SRB setup on common channel (RAN1797 needs to be active)
-PS RAB setup from idle when RRC setup is done on Common Channel and the given transport channel includes HS-DSCH (RAN1797 and RAN1762 must be active) 

The following L3 NBAP Signaling is not taken into account: Radio Link deletion related signaling
- state transitions to CELL-DCH to idle/ CELL-FACH/CELL-PCH/URA-PCH
- state transitions to CELL-FACH to idle
The reason is not to count the transitions in reverse direction.

3G-RNC|RNC_5406a.Description:

Processing Set Utilization ratio is based on three conditions: 1) throughput utilization, 2) number of users, and 3) HW utilization for HSUPA. For the purpose of this counter, in each sample period, all conditions are calculated. The one with bigger percentage value is used. 
Note: In case of Flexi Rel1 HW, this counter is not produced at all.

3G-RNC|RNC_5452a.KPI Abbreviation in release WCDMA 21: ATM VCC traf load DL cl 4
3G-RNC|RNC_5452a.Description:
Outgoing ATM layer traffic utilization rate (76% < X < 88 %) for single ATM VC connection. 
The load is measured in RNC egress direction. 
It depends on the selected configuration, which traffic type utilizes one VCC. 
The ATM VCC traffic throughput is compared to the VCC PCR (in the case of CBR connection) or MDCR (in the case of UBR+ connection) to calculate the load [%]. 
If there is dedicated VC connection used for HSDPA, this KPI can be used to follow the HSDPA load over Iub and the same applies to other traffic types as well.

3G-RNC|RNC_5455a.Description:
Incoming ATM layer traffic utilization rate (X  > 88 %) for single ATM VC connection. 
The load is measured in RNC ingress direction. 
It depends on the selected configuration, which traffic type utilizes one VCC. 
The ATM VCC traffic throughput is compared to the VCC PCR (in the case of CBR connection) or MDCR (in the case of UBR+ connection) to calculate the load [%]. 
If there is dedicated VC connection used for HSDPA, this KPI can be used to follow the HSDPA load over Iub and the same applies to other traffic types as well.

2G-BSC|ava_68.Description:
Data service availability (DSA) gives the estimated percentage of on-air GPRS-capable
BTSs that are able to provide the GPRS service. Detects outages in the GPRS and
EGPRS services. Outages may be caused by a fault in hardware or software.
2G-BSC|ava_68.KPI Logical Formula: 100 * ((1 - Subscriber access outage rate) * (1 - Number of no data activity case))
2G-BSC|ava_68.KPI Formula (with NetAct Names):
((100 *( 1-( COUNT (*) WHERE ([PACKET_CH_REQ] >100 AND ([NBR_OF_UL_TBF]+[NO_RADIO_RES_AVA_UL_TBF]) >80 AND ([AVE_DUR_UL_TBF_SUM] =0 OR [AVE_DUR_DL_TBF_SUM] =0)) /COUNT(*) WHERE ([PACKET_CH_REQ] >= 100))
*  1-( COUNT (*) WHERE (([AVE_TCH_BUSY_FULL]+[AVE_TCH_BUSY_HALF]) >=0.2 AND ([AVE_GPRS_CHANNELS_SUM] >0) AND ([PACKET_CH_REQ] =0 OR [TCH_CALL_REQ] >10)) / COUNT(*) WHERE (([AVE_TCH_BUSY_FULL] + [AVE_TCH_BUSY_HALF]) >= 0.2) AND [AVE_GPRS_CHANNELS_SUM] > 0) AND ([TCH_CALL_REQ] > 10)))))
2G-BSC|ava_68.Formula Note: Known problems:In some situations base station can receive 11-bit RACH burst having legal establishment cause but no real mobile on cell  (e.g. noise). This will cause TBF establishments in BSC and also increment of packet_ch_req counter. In bad radio condition this amount can be more than 100. Official statement is that the number of ghost packet channel request messages cannot be bigger than 100 during one measurement period but it has been noticed that this limit can be exceed in some situations. It is proposed that the limit used in this condition "packet_ch_req >= 100" shall be set (bigger than 100) based on the real network conditions. 100 will be enough in many cases, however.
2G-BSC|ava_68.Time Summary Levels: Total; week; weeklyBH; day; dailyBH; hour

2G-BSC|ava_129.Description:
Traffic channel timeslot availability as the percentage of configured resources. Includes both circuit switched and packet switched TSLs.
Timeslots locked by power save features RG301936 Intelligent MCPA TRX Power Down or BSS20984 2G TRX Automatic Power Down are excluded in denominator AVE_TCH_TSL_LOCKED_POWER_DOWN, because timeslots locked by these features are not counted as available but are counted in the total timeslot unavailable counter (ave_non_avail_tch_timeslot).

The counters in this formula are sampled every 20 seconds. It is normal that during the shutdown or powerup of the TRXs due to the Power Save Features a discrepancy occurs between the total time slots unavailable and the ones locked by the feature originating a slight and sporadic decrease in the KPI (close to 100%, but not 100%).

If TRXs are locked and BTSs and BCFs are unlocked, the TCH TSLs appear as unavailable. Thus both the system and the user can affect this KPI.
The KPI has to be counted separately different TRX types (trx_type: 0 = normal area ,1 = extended area, 2 = super-extended area).

2G-BSC|dcr_5a.KPI Name: TCH dropped conversation ratio without RE
2G-BSC|dcr_5a.Description:
This KPI tells the ratio of calls dropped while A and B are talking, that is after conn_ack.
Inter-BSC handovers are subtracted in the denominator because they trigger
conver_started. Compensation is 100% true only if the area has no inter-BSC HOs from
outside the area.
2G-BSC|dcr_5a.Formula Note:
Known problems:  See dcr_5.
1)conver_started is not triggered for call re-establishments.
dropped_calls is triggered once for the first re-establishment. After that setup_failure is triggered if the call is a dropped call.If a call is ?saved? by re-establishment multiple times, setup_failure will be triggered several times accordingly.
2) Drop call by pre-emption (first priority call request to be established, all TCH seized, lower priority calls on) triggers 
dropped_calls. Therefore this counter does not indicate only technical drops.
Future: In S7 re-establishments can be compensated.
2G-BSC|dcr_5a.Time Summary Levels: Total; week; weeklyBH; day; dailyBH; hour

This KPI is used to monitor the PCU load in terms of received DL Gb over IP traffic vs. Gb processing capacity.
Note that this does not indicate the exact Gb link load as the actual bandwidth is not known.
For the PCU1 and the first release of PCU2 (PDU2-D/U cards) the processing capability in terms of Gb traffic is 2Mbits/s.
For PCU2-E and PCUM cards the capability is higher and KPI values over 100% are possible.

2G-BSC|hfr_2b.Description:
This KPI can be used for dimensioning clusters to provide need capacity for MS mobility.
HO failure in Nokia BSS can occur without the actual HO command.
(for example, there is reason for a HO, but the target cell is full.) This KPI includes both
the failed HOs where the HO command is sent and those where the HO command is not
sent to the MS. HO failures are not visible to end (MS) users.
2G-BSC|hfr_2b.KPI Logical Formula:
HO attempts - successful HOs
        100 * --------------------------------- 
                         HO commands
        
                     successful HOs
        = 100 * (1- --------------   )  
                      HO commands
2G-BSC|hfr_2b.Formula Note: Segment related problems: Does not work on BTS level if a segment of several BTSs is used.
2G-BSC|hfr_2b.Time Summary Levels: Total; week; weeklyBH; day; dailyBH; hour

mobility. Handover failure in Nokia BSS can occur without the actual
HO command. (for example, there is a reason for a HO, but the target cell is full).
Use:
This KPI is used on the area level.

2G-BSC|hfr_55c.Time Summary Levels: Total; week; weeklyBH; day; dailyBH; hour

2G-BSC|hfr_68c.Description:
This KPI defines how big a share of the started handovers are dropped. It indicates the
quality of the handovers. HO drops are visible as dropped calls to end (MS) users.
This KPI does not work on BTS level if the BTS is part of the multisegment. A reason for
this is that an attempt counter triggers for a target BTS only if a HO is successful. In the
case of a handover failure, the attempt counter triggers only for the master BTS.

for TBF sessions. The KPI measures purely the retainability of TBFs and is not
dependent on interfaces and NEs outside BSS.
Note: Not usable on BTS level when common BCCH is used because TBF can start in
one BTS of a segment and end in another.

100-TBF failure % =

100 - 100 * (TBF establishments -Normal TBF releases   
- releases due to flush - releases due to suspend 
- releases due to DTM procedures
---------------------------------------------------   
TBF establishments)

2G-BSC|trf_233c.KPI Name: Average effective ACK GPRS UL throughput per used TSL
2G-BSC|trf_233c.KPI Abbreviation: Avg ef ACK GPRS UL thp us TSL
2G-BSC|trf_233c.Description:
Indicates the impact of radio link quality on net data rate per used timeslot considering
retransmissions and coding scheme selection. The lower the value the poorer the radio
link quality causing retransmissions and use of lower coding schemes.
The numerator does not contain the RLC header bytes neither the does the MAC header
because the aim is to count data volume from the users point of view as close as possible.
The denominator is built on the fact that one timeslot can carry 50 RLC blocks per
second.
Note: Formula assumes that all GRPS unack RLC traffic is using CS1. With PCU2,
GPRS unack RLC traffic can use CS1-4. If there is a significant amount of GRPS unack
RLC traffic with CS2, the formula will give too high values.

GPRS UL payload ACK data in (kilobits)
------------------------------------------------------------- 
GPRS UL time for ACK data transfer (sec)

((SUM(([(No FormulaWithPiId specified)] - [072066])*20 + [(No FormulaWithPiId specified)]*30
+ SUM OVER MCS-11 ([(No FormulaWithPiId specified)])*36
+ SUM OVER MCS-12 ([(No FormulaWithPiId specified)])*50)*8 /1000)
/(SUM([(No FormulaWithPiId specified)] - [072066] + [(No FormulaWithPiId specified)]
+ [072173] + [072174]
+ SUM OVER MCS-11..12([(No FormulaWithPiId specified)] + [079008])) /50))

4G|LTE_5023h.KPI Name: E-UTRAN E-RAB Normal Release Ratio User Perspective
4G|LTE_5023h.KPI Name in previous release: E-UTRAN E-RAB Normal Release Ratio User Perspective
4G|LTE_5023h.KPI Abbreviation: E-RAB norm Rel R EPC init
4G|LTE_5023h.KPI Abbreviation in previous release: E-RAB norm Rel R EPC init
4G|LTE_5023h.Description: This KPI describes the ratio of normally released E-RABs from user perspective. This KPI is corresponding to a Connection Completion Ratio.
4G|LTE_5023h.Description in previous release: This KPI describes the ratio of normally released E-RABs from user perspective. This KPI is corresponding to a Connection Completion Ratio.
4G|LTE_5023h.Note:
1.	Each bearer of the Bearer to be Released List IE is counted
2.	E-RAB releases due to No Radio Resources Available initiated by eNB are counted as abnormal releases from user perspective.
3.	E-RAB releases due to double S1 which are counted within the ERAB_REL_DOUBLE_S1 are considered as normal releases from end user perspective. Typical scenario such a case may happen is  when VoLTE call (a session in general)  is ongoing, UE  losses synchronization and send RRC reestablishment on an unprepared target cell which will send RRC reestablishment rejection to UE. UE will go to idle state and send new RRC request on target cell. When MME receives service request in Initial UE message via target cell followed by sending Initial Context setup Request message to eNB, the MME will already have UE context from source cell  (T_RLF still not expired at source cell) so will send UE context release command (RNL UE connectivity lost cause). The E-RABs that are re-established in target cell via sending Initial Context setup response message to MME are then not perceived in source cell as abnormal but  as normal releases from end user perspective.
4.	In relation to previous point the KPI may have an error in the networks with degraded LTE_5112c.  
5.	It shall be noted that RNL UE connectivity lost  cause is generated for double S1 only by fALU MME. The MME from Cisco and Nokia vendors generate NAS: normal cause for double S1 which means directly contributing to normal releases. The Ericsson MME generates RNL E-UTRAN Generated reason cause for double S1 which is currently not counted within any dedicated counter. Due to this fact the KPI may provide higher values comparing to reality for the network with Ericsson MME. In general, regarding the networks with MME from other vendors than fALU there can be an error as well in case the RNL UE connectivity lost cause generated for some other scenarios than double S1.
6.	In both numerator and denominator of the formula normal E-RAB releases due to successful HO to eHRPD are not counted.
7.	The KPI may provide slightly less values compared to reallity in case in the network environment there is an Ericsson MME used when the ERAB_REL_HO_PART counter is erroneously pegged when E-RABs are not admitted with a cause successful-handover, but in fact in the E-RABs to Release List IE of the S1AP:HANDOVER COMMAND message they were accepted by the MME.

4G|LTE_5119g.KPI Name: E-UTRAN E-RAB Drop Ratio, User Perspective
4G|LTE_5119g.KPI Name in previous release: E-UTRAN E-RAB Drop Ratio, User Perspective
4G|LTE_5119g.Description: This KPI describes the ratio of abnormally released (dropped) E-RABs from user perspective point of view.
4G|LTE_5119g.Description in previous release: This KPI describes the ratio of abnormally released (dropped) E-RABs from user perspective point of view.
4G|LTE_5119g.Note:
1. Each bearer of the "Bearer to be Released List" IE is counted. 
2. User perspective means that, as abnormal E-RAB releases, the releases initiated by eNB and EPC are counted.
3. E-RAB releases due to "No Radio Resources Available" initiated by eNB are counted as abnormal releases from user perspective.
4. E-RAB releases due to double S1 which are counted within the ERAB_REL_DOUBLE_S1 are considered as normal releases from end user perspective. Typical scenario such a case may happen is  when VoLTE call (a session in general) is ongoing, UE  losses synchronization and send RRC reestablishment on an unprepared target cell which will send RRC reestablishment rejection to UE. UE will go to idle state and send new RRC request on target cell. When MME receives service request via target cell, it will already have UE context from source cell  (T_RLF still not expired at source cell) so will send UE context release command (RNL UE connectivity lost cause).In denominator of the formula normal E-RAB releases due to successful HO to eHRPD are not counted.
4G|LTE_5119g.Note in previous release:

3. E-RAB releases due to "No Radio Resources Available" initiated by eNB are counted as abnormal releases from user perspective.
4. E-RAB releases due to double S1 which are counted within the ERAB_REL_DOUBLE_S1 are considered as normal releases from end user perspective. Typical scenario such a case may happen is  when VoLTE call (a session in general) is ongoing, UE  losses synchronization and send RRC reestablishment on an unprepared target cell which will send RRC reestablishment rejection to UE. UE will go to idle state and send new RRC request on target cell. When MME receives service request via target cell, it will already have UE context from source cell  (T_RLF still not expired at source cell) so will send UE context release command (RNL UE connectivity lost cause).In denominator of the formula normal E-RAB releases due to successful HO to eHRPD are not counted.

4G|LTE_5204d.KPI Name: E-UTRAN E-RAB Setup Success Ratio, QCI1
4G|LTE_5204d.KPI Name in previous release: E-UTRAN E-RAB Setup Success Ratio, QCI1
4G|LTE_5204d.Description: The KPI indicates the setup success ratio of the elementary E-RAB setup procedure used to set up the E-RAB between MME and UE for QCI1 DRBs. It indicates E-UTRAN contribution to the network accessibility for the end user, not the whole end-to-end service accessibility.
4G|LTE_5204d.Description in previous release: The KPI indicates the setup success ratio of the elementary E-RAB setup procedure used to set up the E-RAB between MME and UE for QCI1 DRBs. It indicates E-UTRAN contribution to the network accessibility for the end user, not the whole end-to-end service accessibility.
4G|LTE_5204d.Note:
a. For those E-RABs that were temporarily admitted by the eNB and later were released due to overbooking timer expiry are excluded from the nominator of the AdditionalE-RABSetupSuccRate, because they were never used to hand the call over to UTRAN. The setup retry attempts related to additional E-RABs of QCI1 that failed due to ongoing mobility event and also the first setup attempts that failed due to ongoing mobility event  but were followed finally by successful RLF recovery via X2 or S1 (when setup procedure according to 3GPP TS 23.401 shall be done again in target cell) are removed from the denominator of the formula and only first attempts perceived by end user are counted.
b. LTE_5204d may give over-realistic values in high quality networks, where results for E-RAB Normal Releases are near 100% and may sometimes be skipped from one measurement time interval to another, this issue may be even experienced as an avalanche which means it may influence more than 2 intervals (up to infinity). So customer may experience such situation in MT1 100%, MT2 100,05%, MT3 100% ... MT45 99,95%. In such case it is suggested to use LTE_5204c formula where repetitions of E-RAB Setup are counted and there is no subtraction of aborted setup attempt due to mobility, which gives a solid argument that denominator shall almost always be higher than numerator and will very rarely pass 100% due to counting in different measurement time intervals.

3. QCI1 E-RAB releases due to double S1 which are counted within the ERAB_REL_DOUBLE_S1_QCI1 are considered as normal releases from end user perspective. a) The PRE_EMPT_UE_CONTEXT_NON_GBR counter provide the total number of released released UE context due to "Radio resources not available" despite a pre-emption used in the counter name. Those releases are counted as abnormal ones from user perspective.
b) UE context releases due to double S1 which are counted within the UE_CTX_REL_DOUBLE_S1 are considered as normal releases from end user perspective. Typical scenario such a case may happen is  when VoLTE call (a session in general) is ongoing, UE  losses synchronization and send RRC reestablishment on an unprepared target cell which will send RRC reestablishment rejection to UE. UE will go to idle state and send new RRC request on target cell. When MME receives service request via target cell, it will already have UE context from source cell  (T_RLF still not expired at source cell) so will send UE context release command (RNL UE connectivity lost cause).
c) In both numerator and denominator of the formula normal UE Context releases due to successful HO to eHRPD are not counted.

4G|LTE_5570g.Description in previous release: This KPI describes the ratio of a specific E-RAB drop (abnormal release) cause related to all E-RAB releases. Cause: E-RAB active drop ratio with data in the buffer due to RNL Radio Connection with UE Lost cause initiated by eNB.
4G|LTE_5570g.Note:
1. Each bearer of the "Bearer to be Released List" IE is counted. 
2. There is an overlapping in the abnormal E-RABs counted within the LTE_5090f and LTE_5570g but from network planning and optimization point of view it is mandatory to have also an own indicator dealing with active E-RAB drops with data in the buffer only.
3. The formula LTE_5571f is needed to monitor the VoIP Call Drop Ratio.
4. E-RAB releases due to S1 RESET are not counted at all in the LTE_5571f.
5. E-RAB releases due to "No Radio Resources Available" initiated by eNB are counted as normal releases from RAN perspective as they are not real drops resulted from any radio quality problems. 
6. In denominator of the formula normal E-RAB releases due to successful HO to eHRPD are not counted.

4G|LTE_5571g.Description in previous release: This KPI describes the ratio of a specific E-RAB drop (abnormal release) cause related to all E-RAB releases. Cause: E-RAB QCI1 with data in the queue drop ratio, RAN View, RNL Failure with UE Lost.

1. Each bearer of the "Bearer to be Released List" IE is counted. 
2. There is an overlapping in the abnormal E-RABs counted within the LTE_5090f and LTE_5570g but from network planning and optimization point of view it is mandatory to have also an own indicator dealing with active E-RAB drops with data in the buffer only.

5. E-RAB releases due to "No Radio Resources Available" initiated by eNB are counted as normal releases from RAN perspective as they are not real drops resulted from any radio quality problems.

4G|LTE_5747a.Description: This KPI indicates how much of the user data volume is transmitted over the bandwidth of used PRBs.
4G|LTE_5747a.Description in previous release: This KPI indicates how much of the user data volume is transmitted over the bandwidth of used PRBs.
4G|LTE_5747a.Note:
1. KPI gives Spectral efficiency in bits/s/Hz where ([PDCP_SDU_VOL_DL] *8/(#  of TTIs in the measurement period/1000)) represents = (PDCP SDU volume in DL[bits]/Measurement period duration [seconds]) and ( [PRB_USED_PDSCH]*180 000) /(#  of TTIs in the measurement period)) represents (averaged # of PRBs used for PDSCH * 180 000 [Hz]) in the logical formula. Used PRBs also contain SRB which do not contribute to the volume. Hence, spectral efficiency might show slightly worse values depending on the ratio of SRB to DRB.
2. This KPI shall be valid only for cells which are counting PCell UEs. This means that SCell UEs and their respective data usage in the monitored cell shall NOT be counted.
3. This KPI shall be valid for PCell and SCell data volume for Intra-side CA and Inter-side CA. This means that in the monitored cell the PDCP data volume shall be counted which is designated for the related PCell and SCell(s) for which the given PCell UE is camped.
4. This may lead to a situation that for the cells acting as SCell(s) mainly the KPI value might be decreased significantly.
5. Also in case of simultaneous LTE-NR DSS usage and CA usage it may happen that LTE may increase its PRB usage and lower down its PDCP data volume, because majority of used PRBs were given to SCell UEs, which are not counted in the PDCP volume counter.

4G|LTE_5994b.Description: This KPI describes the ratio of abnormally released (dropped) QCI2 E-RABs from RAN point of view.
4G|LTE_5994b.Description in previous release: This KPI describes the ratio of abnormally released (dropped) QCI2 E-RABs from RAN point of view.
4G|LTE_5994b.Note:
1.	Each QCI2 bearer of the Bearer to be Released List IE is counted. 
2.	RAN point of view means that as abnormal E-RAB drops only those ones initiated by eNB are counted.
3.	In the denominator of the formula normal and abnormal E-RAB releases except the successful intra LTE and inter RAT HO are counted. 
4.	QCI2 E-RAB releases due to S1 RESET are not counted at all.
5.	The KPI may provide slightly higher values compared to reallity in case in the network environment there is an Ericsson MME used when the ERAB_REL_HO_PART_QCI2 counter is erroneously pegged when E-RABs are not admitted with a cause successful-handover, but in fact in the E-RABs to Release List IE of the S1AP:HANDOVER COMMAND message they were accepted by the MME.

4G|LTE_6215c.Description: This KPI describes the ratio of a specific E-RAB drop (abnormal release) cause related to all E-RAB releases for Cat-M UEs.
4G|LTE_6215c.Description in previous release: This KPI describes the ratio of a specific E-RAB drop (abnormal release) cause related to all E-RAB releases for Cat-M UEs.
4G|LTE_6215c.Note:
1. Each bearer of the "Bearer to be Released List" IE is counted. 
2. E-RAB releases due to "No Radio Resources Available" initiated by eNB are counted as normal releases from RAN perspective as they are not real drops resulted from any radio quality problems.
3. All Initial and Additional E-RABs are being counted within Retainability KPIs.
4. E-RAB releases due to double S1 for Cat-M UEs  which are counted within the ERAB_REL_DS1_LTEM are considered as normal releases from end user perspective. Typical scenario such a case may happen is  when VoLTE call (a session in general)  is ongoing, UE  losses synchronization and send RRC reestablishment on an unprepared target cell which will send RRC reestablishment rejection to UE. UE will go to idle state and send new RRC request on target cell. When MME receives service request via target cell, it will already have UE context from source cell  (T_RLF still not expired at source cell) so will send UE context release command (RNL UE connectivity lost cause).

4G|LTE_6231c.Note: E-RAB releases due to double S1 for Cat-M UEs which are counted within the ERAB_REL_DS1_LTEM are considered as normal releases from end user perspective. Typical scenario such a case may happen is  when VoLTE call (a session in general)  is ongoing, UE  losses synchronization and send RRC reestablishment on an unprepared target cell which will send RRC reestablishment rejection to UE. UE will go to idle state and send new RRC request on target cell. When MME receives service request via target cell, it will already have UE context from source cell  (T_RLF still not expired at source cell) so will send UE context release command (RNL UE connectivity lost cause).

4G|LTE_6451a.Description in previous release: This KPI describes the ratio of a specific VoLTE E-RAB drop (abnormal release) cause related to all VoLTE E-RAB releases for Cat-M UEs.
4G|LTE_6451a.Note:
1. Each bearer of the "Bearer to be Released List" IE is counted. 
2. E-RAB releases due to �No Radio Resources Available� initiated by eNB are counted as normal releases from RAN perspective as they are not real drops resulted from any radio quality problems.
3. All Initial and Additional E-RABs are being counted within Retainability KPIs.
4. E-RAB releases due to double S1 for Cat-M UEs  which are counted within the ERAB_REL_DS1_LTEM are considered as normal releases from end user perspective. Typical scenario such a case may happen is  when VoLTE call (a session in general)  is ongoing, UE  losses synchronization and send RRC reestablishment on an unprepared target cell which will send RRC reestablishment rejection to UE. UE will go to idle state and send new RRC request on target cell. When MME receives service request via target cell, it will already have UE context from source cell  (T_RLF still not expired at source cell) so will send UE context release command (RNL UE connectivity lost cause).

4G|LTE_6898a.Note:
1.	Each bearer of the "Bearer to be Released List" IE is counted. 
2.	There is an overlapping in the abnormal E-RABs counted within the LTE_5090f and LTE_5570g but from network planning and optimization point of view it is mandatory to have also an own indicator dealing with active E-RAB drops with data in the buffer only.
3.	The formula LTE_5571f is needed to monitor the VoIP Call Drop Ratio.
4.	E-RAB releases due to pre-emption initiated by eNB are counted as normal releases from RAN perspective as they are not real drops resulted from any radio quality problems. 
5.	In denominator of the formula normal E-RAB releases due to successful HO to eHRPD are not counted.

4G|LTE_6952e.KPI Name: E-UTRAN Normal Release Ratio per EN-DC UE Context
4G|LTE_6952e.KPI Name in previous release: E-UTRAN Normal Release Ratio per EN-DC UE Context
4G|LTE_6952e.Description: This KPI indicates E-UTRAN Normal Release Ratio per EN-DC UE Context.
4G|LTE_6952e.Description in previous release: This KPI indicates E-UTRAN Normal Release Ratio per EN-DC UE Context.
4G|LTE_6952e.Note:
1. In case LTE5348 is enabled the successful intra-LTE handovers shall be excluded from counting with the following note: X2AP: 'SgNB Release Request message sent from the source MeNB to the SgNB with 'RNL:MCG Mobility' cause for the SCG split bearers when IE 'UE Context Kept Indicator' was included in the previously HoRequestACK message received from target MeNB, and HO was successfully completed'.
	2. The Inter-eNB X2 HO with EN-DC keeping counters (SGNB_REL_TMENB_HO_X2_CNC and SGNB_REL_TMENB_HO_X2_PR_F) are subtracted from the denominator in order to avoid double counting of the same release which may happen on the source side and it is for the source MeNB to decide whether EN-DC connectivity shall be released or not.
	3. Counter SGNB_ABN_REL_TMENB_HO_X2_EX_F shall not be subtracted from SGNB_TOT_REL_INIT_MENB, because from the source MeNB the handover was successful and shall not be counted on the source side, which means it is up to target MeNB to decide to release the EN-DC connection or not.

1.Each bearer of the "Bearer to be Released List" IE is counted. 
2.There is an overlapping in the abnormal E-RABs counted within the LTE_5090f and LTE_5570g but from network planning and optimization point of view it is mandatory to have also an own indicator dealing with active E-RAB drops with data in the buffer only.

5.E-RAB releases due to pre-emption initiated by eNB are counted as normal releases from RAN perspective as they are not real drops resulted from any radio quality problems. 
6.In denominator of the formula normal E-RAB releases due to successful HO to eHRPD are not counted.

5G|NR_5050b.KPI Name: 5G Average estimated F1 round trip delay between CU and MAC DU
5G|NR_5050b.KPI Name in previous release: 5G Average estimated F1 round trip delay between CU and MAC DU
5G|NR_5050b.KPI Abbreviation: Avg F1 rnd trip delay CU MAC DU
5G|NR_5050b.KPI Abbreviation in previous release: Avg F1 rnd trip delay CU MAC DU
5G|NR_5050b.Description:
This KPI shows the average estimated F1 round trip delay between CU and MAC DU, measured on gNB and per DU. It is the time:
- Starting when the PDCP PDU packet is sent by CU over F1 (PDCP PDU packet has left CU)
Then, this PDCP PDU packet is going until MAC PDU (of DU). When the 1st segment is ready to be sent  on the air for the first time (excluding repetitions), the MAC PDU sends a DDDS to CU.      
- And ending when the DDDS (sent by the MAC PDU) message is received by CU over F1 to acknowledge the packet (removed from CU buffer).
Note: 
-	We can consider that the time to process the DDDS message is equivalent to a PDU message received on CU over F1 and the PDU was sent by MAC PDU.

5G|NR_5055a.KPI Name: 5G Residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PDSCH
5G|NR_5055a.KPI Name in previous release: 5G Residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PDSCH
5G|NR_5055a.Description:
This KPI shows the residual Block Error Ratio (BLER) for PDSCH. Residual BLER is defined as the ratio between the number of failed transmissions after the MAX harq retransmission reached and the number of packets to transmit, that is, the 1st HARQ transmissions.
In real-time monitoring, the HARQ feedback might be received in a diferent measurement period than the initial transmission. For that reason, the initial transmissions in the formula are calculated as the successful transmissions plus the unsuccessful transmissions.
HARQ feedback DTX is considered as unsuccessful.

5G|NR_5073a.KPI Abbreviation in previous release: NSA IntergNB PSC chng exec SR tgNB
5G|NR_5073a.Description:
This KPI shows the inter gNB PSCell change execution success ratio calculated on the target gNB. The execution is considered successful when target gNB receives the X2AP: SGNB RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE sent by LTE eNB (with Configuration successfully applied IE) upon SN Change trigger. The execution attempts are given by the number of  X2AP: SGNB ADDITION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE sent to LTE eNB, upon SN Change trigger.
Intra frequency and inter frequency PSCell changes are taken into account.
5G|NR_5073a.Description in previous release:

The execution is considered successful when target gNB receives the X2AP: SGNB RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE sent by LTE eNB (with Configuration successfully applied IE) upon SN Change trigger. The execution attempts are given by the number of  X2AP: SGNB ADDITION REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE sent to LTE eNB, upon SN Change trigger.
Intra frequency and inter frequency PSCell changes are taken into account.

5G|NR_5074a.Description:
This KPI shows the inter gNB PSCell change total success ratio calculated in the target gNB. The total success ratio is calculated from the successful execution over the preparation attempts. The preparation attempts are the number of X2AP: SGNB ADDITION REQUEST messages received from LTE eNB upon SN Change trigger. The execution successes are given by the number of X2AP: SGNB RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE messages (with Configuration successfully applied IE) sent by LTE eNB to the target gNB, upon SN Change trigger.
Intra frequency and inter frequency PSCell changes are taken into account.

The preparation attempts are the number of X2AP: SGNB ADDITION REQUEST messages received from LTE eNB upon SN Change trigger. The execution successes are given by the number of X2AP: SGNB RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE messages (with Configuration successfully applied IE) sent by LTE eNB to the target gNB, upon SN Change trigger.
Intra frequency and inter frequency PSCell changes are taken into account.
5G|NR_5074a.KPI Logical Formula: IntergNB PSC chng tot SR tgNB = 100 * IntergNB PSC chng exec succ / IntergNB PSC chng prep att

5G|NR_5261a.Description: This KPI shows the average DL PDCP SDU end user throughput per DRB per QoS group 1. It is given as ratio of the total transmitted DL PDCP SDU volume (regardless if using only primary- or also supplemental aggregated carriers) over NR leg (SA or NSA option 3x) and LTE leg (NSA option 3x), and time interval with data in the buffer in gNB CU and gNB DU in case of NR leg (SA or NSA option 3x) and eNB in case of LTE leg (NSA option 3x) related to the QoS group 1 DRBs in the observed period.
5G|NR_5261a.Description in previous release: This KPI shows the average DL PDCP SDU end user throughput per DRB per QoS group 1. It is given as ratio of the total transmitted DL PDCP SDU volume (regardless if using only primary- or also supplemental aggregated carriers) over NR leg (SA or NSA option 3x) and LTE leg (NSA option 3x), and time interval with data in the buffer in gNB CU and gNB DU in case of NR leg (SA or NSA option 3x) and eNB in case of LTE leg (NSA option 3x) related to the QoS group 1 DRBs in the observed period.
5G|NR_5261a.Note:
1. Operator has an option to configure volume and duration of the bursts to be excluded from counting via the following parameters:NRBTS/NRDRB/durationThresDiscard, and NRBTS/NRDRB/volThresDiscard

5G|NR_5635a.KPI Name: 5G SA 5QI1 QoS Flow Drop Ratio - User view (double-Ng mapped to 'UE lost')
5G|NR_5635a.KPI Name in previous release: 5G SA 5QI1 QoS Flow Drop Ratio - User view (double-Ng mapped to 'UE lost')
5G|NR_5635a.Description: This KPI shows the ratio of the number of abnormally released 5QI1 QoS flow attempts initiated by gNB and AMF to total number of 5QI1 QoS flow release attempts (gNB and AMF initiated).
5G|NR_5635a.Description in previous release: This KPI shows the ratio of the number of abnormally released 5QI1 QoS flow attempts initiated by gNB and AMF to total number of 5QI1 QoS flow release attempts (gNB and AMF initiated).
5G|NR_5635a.Note: It is valid for AMF when the NG_FLOW_REL_AMF_UE_LOST_5QI1 is triggered with respective number of 5QI1 QoS flow related to sending of UE Context Release Command to the source cell gNB in case of 'double Ng' scenario, when Radio Link Failure occurs during an ongoing 5QI1 QoS flow call and RRC Connection Re-establishment attempt fails on target or another cell. If then the UE does a new RRC Connection the 5QI1 QoS flow is set-up during Initial Context Setup in the target or other cell. However, when AMF receives that service request with the Initial UE message through the target or other cell, it realizes that it already has the same UE Context but from the source cell (it has not been released yet as T-RLF is still running). In such case, AMF sends UE Context Release Command to the source cell. As the 5QI1 QoS flow has been successfully setup in the target or other cell, the 5QI1 QoS flow release in the source cell is not perceived as a drop (abnormal release) by the end user, as the service has been sustained with some interruption time and can't be considered as a drop in the 5QI1 QoS flow Drop Ratio from end user perspective. From network perspective it makes still sense to consider it as a drop to further optimize the network to reduce the interruption time to an acceptable value.

3G-BTS|RNC_1879e.Description:
The average active HS-DSCH MAC-d throughput from end user perspective, calculated
as the HSDPA MAC-d throughput at BTS, divided by the active HS-DSCH time
multiplied by the active users.  

The active time refers to the scheduled TTIs, i.e. when sending data. 
The active users refers to the number of users with data in the allocated buffer. 
Allocated buffer means that the users are scheduled or waiting to be scheduled in a TTI.

The throughput is looked at from MAC-d layer, i.e. how much MAC-d level
data the HS-DSCH is able to successfully transfer to UEs using the scheduled
TTIs, so this considers also the MAC-hs efficiency.

3G-RNC, 3G-BTS|RNC_5204a.KPI Logical Formula in previous release: (IuB PS throughput / Max IuB PS throughput + CS Erl / Max CS Erl) * 100%
3G-RNC, 3G-BTS|RNC_5204a.Formula Note:
IuB PS Throughput = ((T_PS*1.11- T_HSDPA)*(1+SHO_OH) + T_HSDPA), where 1.11 is FP overhead. 

T_PS - Iu-PS average throughput in downlink direction. This KPI results from the combination of GTP-U throughput and Iu-PS throughput counted at NP8S1 or NP2GE interfaces unit, providing the whole figure for combined Iu-PS throughput.

T-HSPA - HSDPA throughput on frame protocol level.

SHO_OH - Soft Handover Overhead in SRNC

CS_Erl - CS Voice, Erlangs.

2G|ava_129.Description:
Traffic channel timeslot availability as the percentage of configured resources. Includes both circuit switched and packet switched TSLs.
Timeslots locked by power save features RG301936 Intelligent MCPA TRX Power Down or BSS20984 2G TRX Automatic Power Down are excluded in denominator AVE_TCH_TSL_LOCKED_POWER_DOWN, because timeslots locked by these features are not counted as available but are counted in the total timeslot unavailable counter (ave_non_avail_tch_timeslot).

The counters in this formula are sampled every 20 seconds. It is normal that during the shutdown or powerup of the TRXs due to the Power Save Features a discrepancy occurs between the total time slots unavailable and the ones locked by the feature originating a slight and sporadic decrease in the KPI (close to 100%, but not 100%).

If TRXs are locked and BTSs and BCFs are unlocked, the TCH TSLs appear as unavailable. Thus both the system and the user can affect this KPI.
The KPI has to be counted separately different TRX types (trx_type: 0 = normal area ,1 = extended area, 2 = super-extended area).

2G|ava_68.Formula Note: Known problems:In some situations base station can receive 11-bit RACH burst having legal establishment cause but no real mobile on cell  (e.g. noise). This will cause TBF establishments in BSC and also increment of packet_ch_req counter. In bad radio condition this amount can be more than 100. Official statement is that the number of ghost packet channel request messages cannot be bigger than 100 during one measurement period but it has been noticed that this limit can be exceed in some situations. It is proposed that the limit used in this condition "packet_ch_req >= 100" shall be set (bigger than 100) based on the real network conditions. 100 will be enough in many cases, however.

2G|dcr_5b.Description:
This KPI tells the ratio of calls dropped while A and B are talking, that is after conn_ack.
Inter-BSC handovers are subtracted in the denominator because they trigger
conver_started. Compensation is 100% true only if the area has no inter-BSC HOs from
outside the area.
2G|dcr_5b.Description in previous release:
This KPI tells the ratio of calls dropped while A and B are talking, that is after conn_ack.
Inter-BSC handovers are subtracted in the denominator because they trigger
conver_started. Compensation is 100% true only if the area has no inter-BSC HOs from
outside the area.
2G|dcr_5b.Formula Note:
Known problems: See dcr_5.
1) conver_started is not triggered for call re-establishments.
dropped_calls is triggered once for the first re-establishment. After that setup_failure is triggered if the  call is a dropped call.
 If a call is ?saved? by re-establishment multiple times, setup_failure will be triggered several times accordingly.
2) Drop call by pre-emption (first priority call request to be established, all TCH seized, lower priority calls on) triggers 
dropped_calls. Therefore this counter does not indicate only technical drops.

This KPI is used to monitor the PCU load in terms of received DL Gb over IP traffic vs. Gb processing capacity.
Note that this does not indicate the exact Gb link load as the actual bandwidth is not known.
For the PCU1 and the first release of PCU2 (PDU2-D/U cards) the processing capability in terms of Gb traffic is 2Mbits/s.
For PCU2-E and PCUM cards the capability is higher and KPI values over 100% are possible.

quality of the handovers. HO drops are visible as dropped calls to end (MS) users.

this is that an attempt counter triggers for a target BTS only if a HO is successful. In the
case of a handover failure, the attempt counter triggers only for the master BTS.

or TCH capacity (CS traffic high).

may be that the territory has been smaller than the default setting defines (CS use). The
PCU will not make an upgrade request. This is because the CS side will return the
default channels back to the PS territory as soon as the CS load allows that.

bcf_type: CM parameter
Definition: With this parameter you identify the type of the BTS site.

NOTE:
Modification of the BTS site type is possible only between the 2nd generation and Talk-family site types and from the 2nd generation or Talk-family site types to UltraSite site and Talk-family or UltraSite site types to Flexi EDGE type. The modification from the UltraSite or Flexi EDGE back to the 2nd generation or Talk-family site types is not possible.
Modification between BTSplus and other site types is not possible.
Modification from UltraSite or Flexi EDGE site type to Flexi Multiradio BTS site type is possible but not vice versa.

NOTE: Parameter is valid only for BTSplus site type

2G|trf_122b.Description:
This KPI indicates TCH use % (sampling interval 480 ms) for half rate AMR.

bcf_type: CM parameter
Definition: With this parameter you identify the type of the BTS site.

NOTE:
Modification of the BTS site type is possible only between the 2nd generation and Talk-family site types and from the 2nd generation or Talk-family site types to UltraSite site and Talk-family or UltraSite site types to Flexi EDGE type. The modification from the UltraSite or Flexi EDGE back to the 2nd generation or Talk-family site types is not possible.
Modification between BTSplus and other site types is not possible.
Modification from UltraSite or Flexi EDGE site type to Flexi Multiradio BTS site type is possible but not vice versa.

Range:  0 (2nd Generation), 1 (Talk-family), 2 (PrimeSite), 3 (MetroSite), 4 (InSite), 5 (UltraSite), 6 (Flexi EDGE), 7 (BTSplus), 8 (Flexi Multiradio) 

IMREPS: CM parameter
Definition: With this parameter you specify the granularity in which the radio measurements have to be transmitted on the A-bis interface in case they are enabled (e.g 8 = 1/8).

NOTE: Parameter is valid only for BTSplus site type
 
Range: 1..254
Default value =8

2G|trf_161j.Description:
Indicates the amount of resources (timeslots) the EGPRS traffic data consumes, on
average, during the period. This information is useful, for example, in estimating the
need for capacity extension. 50 blocks/sec/TSL is used to estimate the timeslots.
For area level, this formula should be first collected for all BTSs in the area. Then, the
results should be summed up for the area.

2G|trf_233c.Description:
Indicates the impact of radio link quality on net data rate per used timeslot considering
retransmissions and coding scheme selection. The lower the value the poorer the radio
link quality causing retransmissions and use of lower coding schemes.
The numerator does not contain the RLC header bytes neither the does the MAC header
because the aim is to count data volume from the users point of view as close as possible.
The denominator is built on the fact that one timeslot can carry 50 RLC blocks per
second.
Note: Formula assumes that all GRPS unack RLC traffic is using CS1. With PCU2,
GPRS unack RLC traffic can use CS1-4. If there is a significant amount of GRPS unack
RLC traffic with CS2, the formula will give too high values.

2G|trf_235b.Description:
Indicates the impact of radio link quality on net data rate per used timeslot considering
retransmissions and coding scheme selection. The lower the value the poorer the radio
link quality causing retransmissions and use of lower coding schemes.
The numerator does not contain the RLC header bytes neither the does the MAC
header because the aim is to count data volume from the users point of view as close
as possible. The denominator is built on the fact that one timeslot can carry 50 RLC
blocks per second.
Note: Formula assumes that all GRPS unack RLC traffic is using CS1. With PCU2,
GPRS unack RLC traffic can use CS1-4. If there is a significant amount of GRPS unack
RLC traffic with CS2, the formula will give too high values.
